transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, hi. Well, I'm here because... I don't know, lately I've just started catching myself thinking that it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up in the morning. Which is a struggle anyway because my alarm goes off at 5:30. I teach secondary school, and the kids this year are just... they're so distracted. I had to confiscate three smartphones just yesterday. I don't even know why parents buy them those things so young, you know? When I was their age, we just passed notes on actual paper. 

But, um... anyway, the drive home from the school is pretty long, and lately I just sit in traffic and wonder whether my family and my students would just be better off without me. Which is awful to think about. My husband has been trying to get me to try this new meal prep delivery thing to save time during the week, so he's trying to help, but... I don't know, where was I? Oh, right. Those thoughts just really scare me. I don't want to act on them or anything, but they just keep popping into my head while I'm driving.
Have you ever experienced a period of time before when you felt this way, with similar thoughts or a persistently low mood?

Um, no, not really. I don't think so. I mean, I've had stressful times, obviously. Like when I was doing my student teaching for my bachelor's degree. That was a total nightmare. My supervising teacher, Mrs. Gable, she was just... so strict. She used to make me re-do my lesson plans if the margins weren't exactly one inch. Can you imagine? Who even checks margins on a printed lesson plan? And she always wore this overpowering floral perfume that gave me a terrible headache. It smelled exactly like the potpourri my grandmother used to keep in a little crystal bowl in her guest bathroom. My grandma had this beautiful house out in the country, and we used to go there every summer... the porch wrapped all the way around, and she had these big wooden rocking chairs. 

But, um... wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling like this before. No, I don't think I've ever had these kinds of thoughts or felt this low in the past. It's all just really new and weird for me.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried a lot of the time, even when there isn't a specific reason for it?

Um... anxious? I don't know if I'd say anxious, really. I mean, I worry about things, sure. Like, I worry about the curriculum changes they're trying to push through the school board next year. They want us to completely overhaul the way we teach history, and it's just... it's absurd. They expect us to just throw out years of material. I spent three weeks last summer perfectly organizing my binders. I color-code everything, you know? Blue for exams, yellow for quizzes, green for handouts. I buy those specific tabs from that one office supply store... you know the one, right by the mall? The mall that used to have that amazing pretzel place, but they closed it down during the pandemic. Which was so sad, my husband and I used to go there on Saturdays just to get the cinnamon sugar ones. He actually tried to make them at home once, but he used way too much yeast and the dough just exploded all over the counter... 

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. Um, anxiety. No, I don't think I'm worried all the time for no reason. Just the normal stuff, I guess. It's really just the... the dark thoughts that are bothering me.
Can you recall if you’ve ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Um, yeah, I guess so. The last few weeks have been exactly like that. I just... I don't care about the things I usually love doing. Like, I play in this recreational softball league on Thursdays, and I've been in this book club for three years. We meet on the first Tuesday of every month. The lady who hosts it, Brenda, she always makes these elaborate charcuterie boards. She gets the fancy cheeses from this little artisanal shop downtown. The one right next to the antique store where I found this gorgeous mid-century modern lamp for my living room. I had to rewire it myself, which was terrifying, but it looks so good. My husband said I was crazy for buying it because the lampshade was slightly stained, but I found a replacement online that matched perfectly...

Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, losing interest. Yeah, I used to really look forward to softball and book club, and working in my garden on the weekends. I even run the robotics club at school, which used to be the highlight of my week. But lately, I just... I mostly just go through the motions. Or I just cancel and stay home. None of it feels enjoyable anymore. It just feels like another chore on my list, you know?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite, sleep, or energy levels recently? Or maybe trouble concentrating on tasks or feeling more guilty than usual?

Um, well, my appetite has definitely been weird. Most school days I just completely forget to eat, or I just avoid it until late in the afternoon. Which is funny, because I used to always bring these elaborate bento boxes for lunch. I got really into meal prepping a couple of years ago. I bought all these glass containers with the little bamboo lids from this online store that sells eco-friendly kitchen stuff. I was trying to cut down on single-use plastics, you know? Because I watched this documentary about the ocean and the sea turtles, and it just broke my heart. My husband and I actually went snorkeling in Hawaii on our honeymoon, and we saw a sea turtle. It was just gliding through the water, so peaceful. We stayed at this resort that had a massive infinity pool, and the breakfast buffet was incredible. They had this fresh papaya that was just... so sweet. 

But, um... oh, right, eating. Yeah, I don't really eat much during the day anymore. And over the past year, my clothes have gotten noticeably looser. I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything, but my favorite pair of work slacks—the navy blue ones I got from that outlet mall—they're practically falling off me now. I had to buy a new belt, this braided leather one, just to keep them up. It's just strange, I guess. I just don't have the energy to care about food right now.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing on tasks lately, like difficulty thinking clearly or making decisions, even about small things?

Um, yeah, focusing has been really hard lately. Especially with school stuff. Like, I'll sit down to grade, and I’ll read the exact same student response three or four times and still not have a clue what score to give it. Which is so frustrating because I usually breeze through grading. I use these specific purple felt-tip pens. I never use red—red is just so aggressive, you know? I read this article a few years ago about color psychology and how red ink makes kids feel defeated, so I switched to purple. I have to order them special from this stationery website. They ship them from Japan, I think. Or maybe Korea? I'm not sure, but the packaging is always so cute, they put a little origami crane in the box every time. I tried to learn origami once, during a rainy weekend. I bought a whole book on it, but the paper kept tearing when I tried to make the frog. The frog is supposed to actually jump if you press on its back, which I thought would be so fun to show my nephew. He just turned seven and he's obsessed with anything that jumps or crawls. We got him a little bug-catching kit for his birthday...

Sorry, my brain just keeps drifting off. What were we talking about? Oh, right, thinking clearly. Yeah, it's not just grading. Making decisions is just as bad right now. Even the simplest choices feel impossible. Like, I had to figure out which lab supplies to order for the upcoming semester, and just picking out basic things stalled me for an entire hour. I just sat there staring at the supply catalog, completely unable to choose.
Have you ever had a period in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for two weeks or more, before this recent episode?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days, obviously. Everyone has bad days. Like when my basement flooded last spring. That was a nightmare. The sump pump just completely gave out during this massive thunderstorm. We had to rip up all the carpet, and it was this really nice plush carpet we had just put in two years ago. We bought it from this local flooring place because the owner’s daughter was in one of my science classes, and I like to support local businesses, you know? She was such a bright girl, she did this amazing project on hydroponics. She actually built a working system out of PVC pipes and a fish tank. I was so impressed, I recommended her for the county science fair. She ended up getting second place, which was huge because the kid who won first place had parents who were both engineers at NASA or something. So it hardly seemed fair. But anyway, the carpet was completely ruined, and it smelled like mildew for weeks, even after we ran three dehumidifiers non-stop. 

But, um... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, feeling down like this before. No, nothing like this. Even when the basement flooded, I was stressed, but I still wanted to do things. This is... this is different. I've never felt like this before.
Can you tell me if there was ever a time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two consecutive weeks?

Um, well, like I said, I haven't really felt this down before, but as far as losing interest in things... yeah. That's definitely happening right now. I used to look forward to so much stuff. Like, I play in this recreational softball league. Or, I used to. I play second base. I got this really great new glove at the start of last season. It's genuine leather, and I spent weeks breaking it in with shaving cream and wrapping it with rubber bands around a baseball. My dad taught me how to do that when I was in Little League. He was our coach for three years, and he always used to bring orange slices in this huge orange Igloo cooler. You know the ones with the little white push-button spout? We had this one game where the spout broke and Gatorade went everywhere, all over the backseat of his station wagon. It was sticky for literally years. We tried everything to get it out, even rented a steam cleaner from the grocery store. The grocery store near my house actually has a really good bakery section. They make these sourdough boules that are just incredible if you toast them with a little bit of salted butter...

Sorry, um, where was I? Oh, right, softball. Yeah, and my book club, too. And my garden. I usually love my garden. And the robotics club I sponsor at school. But lately... I don't know. I just go through the motions if I even show up at all. Mostly I just cancel. None of it feels enjoyable anymore. It just feels like a chore.
Have you ever experienced a time before this recent period where you felt persistently down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Um, well, like I was saying before... no, I really don't think I've ever felt this way before. I mean, I've had times where I was stressed, like when I was getting my teaching credential. Student teaching was so intense. I was placed at this middle school on the other side of town, and the commute was awful. I had to take this one highway that was always under construction. They were widening the lanes or something, but it felt like they were working on it for five years. I used to listen to podcasts just to keep from losing my mind in the traffic. I got really into this one about unsolved historical mysteries. There was this fascinating episode about the Roanoke colony, you know, the one where everyone just disappeared and left that word carved into a tree? Croatoan, I think? It’s so crazy to think about a whole group of people just vanishing without a trace. I actually used that as a writing prompt for my eighth graders once. They came up with the wildest theories—aliens, time travel, giant sea monsters. Kids have such amazing imaginations. I miss when they used to get excited about things like that. One kid even drew this elaborate comic book about... 

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. Um... no, to answer your question, before this recent stuff started, I’ve never had a time where I felt down or didn't want to do things for weeks at a time. This is definitely a first for me.
Have you ever had a time before this recent episode where you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I feel like we just talked about this, right? Um, yeah, no. I haven't. Before all this started recently, I've never had a time where I felt this down or just didn't care about anything for weeks. I mean, sure, I've been sad or whatever for a couple of days, like when my cat died. That was really hard. He was a Maine Coon mix, huge, like twenty pounds, and he had this weird habit of sleeping in the bathroom sink. He would just curl up in there, and you'd have to turn the water on just a tiny bit to get him to move. We got him from a shelter when he was a kitten. Actually, the shelter was having this huge adoption event because they were overflowing with cats from a hoarding situation. It was on the news and everything. They had to bring in volunteers from three different counties just to help process all the animals. I remember it was raining that day, just pouring, and we had to park like three blocks away and walk. My shoes were totally soaked, and they were those canvas slip-ons, so they took forever to dry. I think I ended up throwing them away because they smelled like damp dog and wet cardboard...

But, um, anyway. No. To answer your question again, no. I've never felt like this before this current thing. Never for two weeks straight.

You mentioned that this recent period of feeling down and losing interest in things is new for you. Can you confirm if you have never had a two-week period before this where you felt persistently low or disinterested in your usual activities?

I... I'm sorry, I know I keep getting sidetracked. But yes, I can confirm that. I've definitely never had a two-week period like this before. It's just so strange for me, you know? I'm usually the one organizing everything. Like the staff holiday party last year. I was the head of the committee, and we decided to do a "Winter Wonderland" theme. We spent hours cutting out these intricate paper snowflakes to hang from the ceiling in the cafeteria. We even rented a snow machine, but it ended up just blowing this soapy foam everywhere, and the janitor, Mr. Henderson, was so mad. He had to mop the floor three times to get the residue off. He's been at the school for like thirty years, and he has this enormous collection of antique keys on his keyring. It jingles so loudly you can hear him coming from all the way down the hall. I always wondered what half those keys were even for. Probably doors that don't even exist anymore. I read an article once about a guy who found a hidden room in his house behind a bookshelf, and it was full of old letters from the 1920s... 

Um, but yes. To confirm, no. Never before this.
Can you be certain that you have never had a period lasting at least two weeks in the past where you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, even before this recent episode?

I'm sorry, doctor. I know you keep asking, and I keep rambling. But yes, I am absolutely certain. I've never felt like this for two weeks straight before now. It's really just... this is all new. I don't know why my brain keeps wandering off today. It's like I can't hold a thought in my head. I was trying to grade essays last night, and I just kept staring at the same paragraph about the Industrial Revolution. It was about the textile mills, you know, the ones in Massachusetts? Lowell, I think. They used to hire young women from the farms to come work the looms, and they had to live in these strict boarding houses. I actually visited one of those mills on a field trip when I was in middle school. We took this huge yellow bus, and the driver kept grinding the gears. My friend Sarah and I sat all the way in the back, and we shared a Walkman. We were listening to that one boy band that was super popular... what were they called? They had that one guy with the frosted tips... 

Anyway, sorry. To answer your question, yes, I'm certain. Never before this.
Can you be absolutely certain that you have never had a period lasting at least two weeks in the past where you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, even before this recent episode?

I feel like I'm stuck on a loop today, I'm so sorry. But yes, I am completely sure. I have never, ever had a two-week stretch where I felt this low before all this started. I just... I don't know why I can't seem to just give you a straight answer without bringing up my whole life story. It's like my brain is just grasping at anything other than how I'm actually feeling. Kind of like when I try to get my students to focus on Shakespeare, and they somehow turn the conversation into a debate about whether hotdogs are sandwiches. Which, by the way, took up half of my third period class last Tuesday. One kid, Jason, brought in a whole PowerPoint presentation he made on his phone just to prove his point. He used all these weird transitions, like the one where the slide shatters into a million pieces. He's a smart kid, really good at math, but he refuses to show his work on tests. His mom came in for parent-teacher conferences last month, and she was wearing this amazing vintage coat, like a deep emerald green velvet... 

But yeah. I'm sure. Never before this.
Can you be absolutely certain that you have never had a period lasting at least two weeks in the past where you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, even before this recent episode?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? I'm sorry, I know my brain is all over the place today, but I swear I just answered this exact thing. It's honestly just like when my sophomores ask me what chapters will be on the quiz right after I literally just handed them a study guide. I spent three hours making that study guide last week, too. I even used different fonts for the different sections to make it easier to read. I downloaded this really cute vintage typewriter font off the internet, but then the school printer wouldn't recognize the file, so it just printed everything out in Wingdings. Have you ever tried to read a whole page of Wingdings? It looks like a secret code. When I was little, my brother and I used to make up secret codes using lemon juice as invisible ink. We'd hold the paper up to the lightbulb in his desk lamp to read it, and one time he held it too close and the paper actually caught on fire. My mom was so mad, she grounded us for a week and made us scrub the baseboards with old toothbrushes... 

Um, but yeah. I really don't know what else to tell you. I'm as sure as I can possibly be. I don't have any other answer to give you for that. Did I answer it wrong before, or is there something specific you're looking for me to say?

But, um... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, feeling down like this before. No, nothing like this. Even when the basement flooded, I was stressed, but I still wanted to do things. This is... this is different. I've never felt like this before.

Um, well, like I said, I haven't really felt this down before, but as far as losing interest in things... yeah. That's definitely happening right now. I used to look forward to so much stuff. Like, I play in this recreational softball league. Or, I used to. I play second base. I got this really great new glove at the start of last season. It's genuine leather, and I spent weeks breaking it in with shaving cream and wrapping it with rubber bands around a baseball. My dad taught me how to do that when I was in Little League. He was our coach for three years, and he always used to bring orange slices in this huge orange Igloo cooler. You know the ones with the little white push-button spout? We had this one game where the spout broke and Gatorade went everywhere, all over the backseat of his station wagon. It was sticky for literally years. We tried everything to get it out, even rented a steam cleaner from the grocery store. The grocery store near my house actually has a really good bakery section. They make these sourdough boules that are just incredible if you toast them with a little bit of salted butter...

Sorry, um, where was I? Oh, right, softball. Yeah, and my book club, too. And my garden. I usually love my garden. And the robotics club I sponsor at school. But lately... I don't know. I just go through the motions if I even show up at all. Mostly I just cancel. None of it feels enjoyable anymore. It just feels like a chore.

I got really into this one about unsolved historical mysteries. There was this fascinating episode about the Roanoke colony, you know, the one where everyone just disappeared and left that word carved into a tree? Croatoan, I think? It’s so crazy to think about a whole group of people just vanishing without a trace. I actually used that as a writing prompt for my eighth graders once. They came up with the wildest theories—aliens, time travel, giant sea monsters. Kids have such amazing imaginations. I miss when they used to get excited about things like that. One kid even drew this elaborate comic book about... 

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. Um... no, to answer your question, before this recent stuff started, I’ve never had a time where I felt down or didn't want to do things for weeks at a time. This is definitely a first for me.
